intro.text: This entry describes autosomal dominant deafness-55 (DFNA55). In a mouse study, targeted inactivation of the Tectb gene, encoding a component of the tectorial membrane, caused low-frequency hearing loss (Russell et al., 2007).

checks.claim: The Tectb gene encodes a component of the tectorial membrane.
checks.evidence_quote: The tectorins, Tecta and Tectb, are proteins that are exclusively restricted, within the cochlear duct, to the tectorial membrane
checks.explanation: The paper describes Tectb as a tectorial membrane glycoprotein.

checks.claim: In mice, targeted inactivation of the Tectb gene caused low-frequency hearing loss.
checks.evidence_quote: Although these mice have a low-frequency hearing loss, basilar-membrane and neural tuning are both significantly enhanced in the high-frequency regions of the cochlea
checks.explanation: In Tectb-/- mice, made by targeted deletion of exons 1-4, no protein was detected, and the mice had low-frequency hearing loss.

paragraphs.text: Russell et al. (2007) generated Tectb-null mice by deleting exons 1 through 4 of the Tectb gene by gene targeting. In homozygous mice, Tectb protein was absent from the tectorial membrane, and the striated-sheet matrix was completely missing along the entire length of the membrane. The tectorial membrane remained attached to the organ of Corti, and the distribution of Tecta and otogelin was unchanged. Hensen's stripe was absent in the basal coil. In the apical coil, the tectorial membrane was approximately twice as thick as in controls and had about twice the cross-sectional area; its marginal band was absent and its peripheral edge was frayed. Hair bundle structure was normal.

checks.claim: Russell et al. (2007) generated Tectb-null mice by deleting exons 1 through 4 of the Tectb gene by gene targeting.
checks.evidence_quote: We used gene targeting in embryonic stem cells to delete exons 1-4 of the Tectb gene

checks.claim: In homozygous Tectb-null mice, Tectb protein was absent from the tectorial membrane.
checks.evidence_quote: Tectb was not detected in the tectorial membranes or epithelia of mice homozygous for this deletion

checks.claim: In homozygous Tectb-null mice, the striated-sheet matrix was completely missing along the entire length of the tectorial membrane.
checks.evidence_quote: Transmission electron microscopy revealed a complete absence of striated-sheet matrix throughout the length of the tectorial membrane in Tectb−/− mutant mice

checks.claim: In homozygous Tectb-null mice, the tectorial membrane remained attached to the organ of Corti.
checks.evidence_quote: In the Tectb−/− mutant mice described in this study, the tectorial membrane remains attached to the organ of Corti

checks.claim: In homozygous Tectb-null mice, the distribution of Tecta and otogelin in the tectorial membrane was unchanged.
checks.evidence_quote: The global distributions of Tecta and otogelin in the tectorial membrane were unaffected by the mutation

checks.claim: In homozygous Tectb-null mice, Hensen's stripe was absent in the basal coil of the cochlea.
checks.evidence_quote: there was a noticeable absence of Hensen’s stripe, a longitudinal ridge thought to engage the hair bundles of the inner hair cells
checks.explanation: The absence of Hensen's stripe is described in the basal coil.

checks.claim: In the apical coil of homozygous Tectb-null mice, the tectorial membrane was approximately twice as thick as in controls.
checks.evidence_quote: The thickness of the tectorial membrane in the apical coil of the Tectb−/− mutant was twice that of the heterozygous or wild type mice (72.1±3.5 μm vs. 36.4±1.9 μm

checks.claim: In the apical coil of homozygous Tectb-null mice, the tectorial membrane had about twice the cross-sectional area of controls.
checks.evidence_quote: The cross-sectional area of the tectorial membrane in the distal end of the apical cochlear coil of the Tectb−/− mutant mouse was approximately twice that of heterozygous or wild type mice

checks.claim: In the apical coil of homozygous Tectb-null mice, the marginal band of the tectorial membrane was absent.
checks.evidence_quote: In the apical end of the apical coil, the marginal band was absent and the tectorial membrane had a markedly frayed peripheral edge in the Tectb−/− mutant

checks.claim: In the apical coil of homozygous Tectb-null mice, the peripheral edge of the tectorial membrane was frayed.
checks.evidence_quote: In the apical end of the apical coil, the marginal band was absent and the tectorial membrane had a markedly frayed peripheral edge in the Tectb−/− mutant

checks.claim: Hair bundle structure was normal in homozygous Tectb-null mice.
checks.evidence_quote: In both the apical (Fig. 3c,d) and basal (Fig. 3e,f) coils of the mature cochlea, the form, orientation and density of the hair bundles on inner and outer hair cells were normal.

paragraphs.text: Russell et al. (2007) found that Tectb -/- mice had a distinct hearing loss for frequencies below approximately 20 kHz, with distortion product otoacoustic emission (DPOAE) levels 20 to 30 dB below those of wildtype mice in this low-frequency range. Above 20 kHz, neural sensitivity was near normal. In the high-frequency basal cochlea, both basilar membrane tuning (mean Q10dB 18.9 vs 9.6) and neural tuning (neural masking Q10dB 12.5 to 25.7 vs 5.8 to 8.3) were markedly sharper than in wildtype mice. The authors attributed the sharpened tuning to a reduction in the acting mass of the tectorial membrane and decreased spread of excitation along the cochlea, and concluded that Tectb is essential for low-frequency hearing.

checks.claim: Tectb -/- mice had a distinct hearing loss for frequencies below approximately 20 kHz.
checks.evidence_quote: The enhanced high-frequency tuning in the Tectb−/− mutant mice, therefore, came at the expense of a hearing loss for frequencies below 20 kHz (Fig. 5e).
checks.explanation: The paper reports a distinct low-frequency hearing loss below 20 kHz.

checks.claim: In the low-frequency range below approximately 20 kHz, distortion product otoacoustic emission (DPOAE) levels in Tectb -/- mice were 20 to 30 dB below those of wildtype mice.
checks.evidence_quote: Even with the highest levels of primaries used in these experiments, DPOAE levels in the frequency region below 20 kHz were 20–30 dB less than those recorded from wild type mice (Fig. 5f).

checks.claim: Above 20 kHz, neural sensitivity in Tectb -/- mice was near normal.
checks.evidence_quote: For frequencies above ~ 20 kHz, however, neural sensitivities in wild type and Tectb−/− mutant mice were very similar.
checks.explanation: "Very similar" in the paper matches "near normal" in the draft.

checks.claim: In the high-frequency basal cochlea, basilar membrane tuning in Tectb -/- mice was markedly sharper than in wildtype mice (mean Q10dB 18.9 vs 9.6).
checks.evidence_quote: The bandwidths of tuning curves measured from Tectb−/− mutant mice were, however, less broad than those of wild type mice with a mean Q10 dB (characteristic frequency / bandwidth 10 dB from tip) of 18.9 ± 2.6 (mean ± s.d.) compared with that of 9.6 ± 3.3 for wild type mice.
checks.explanation: The values were measured at the 53 kHz place in the basal turn.

checks.claim: In the high-frequency basal cochlea, neural tuning in Tectb -/- mice was markedly sharper than in wildtype mice (neural masking Q10dB 12.5 to 25.7 vs 5.8 to 8.3).
checks.evidence_quote: Simultaneous masking neural tuning curves closely resemble the tuning properties of single auditory nerve fibers and are more sharply tuned in Tectb−/− mutant mice than in wild type mice (Fig. 5a and Table 1).
checks.explanation: In Table 1, mutant Q10dB values are 12.5, 12.5, 15.9 and 25.7, and wild-type values are 6.25, 8.3, 5.8 and 7.7, so the ranges match. These come from probe tones of 10 to 54 kHz, a wider frequency range than just the basal region.

checks.claim: Russell et al. (2007) attributed the sharper tuning in Tectb -/- mice to a reduction in the acting mass of the tectorial membrane.
checks.evidence_quote: These findings can be attributed to a reduction in the acting mass of the tectorial membrane and reveal a new function for this structure in controlling interactions along the cochlea.

checks.claim: Russell et al. (2007) attributed the sharper tuning in Tectb -/- mice to decreased spread of excitation along the cochlea.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus the enhanced basilar membrane and neural frequency tuning recorded from Tectb−/− mutant mice can be attributed to a reduction in the spread of excitation along the BM and a diminished interaction between adjacent frequency regions in the cochlea.

checks.claim: Russell et al. (2007) concluded that Tectb is essential for low-frequency hearing.
checks.evidence_quote: In this study we show that the presence of Tectb, one of the two major non-collagenous glycoproteins of the mammalian tectorial membrane, is essential for low-frequency hearing.

references.label: Russell et al. (2007)
references.citation: Russell IJ, Legan PK, Lukashkina VA, Lukashkin AN, Goodyear RJ, Richardson GP. Sharpened cochlear tuning in a mouse with a genetically modified tectorial membrane. Nat Neurosci 10: 215-23, 2007. [PubMed: 17220887]
